The world number two, whose round included five birdies and two bogeys in windy conditions, is two shots behind early leader Joost Luiten. Spain's Eugenio Chacarra, who leads McIlroy by 533.93 points in the Race to Dubai standings - with 2,000 available to this week's winner - opened with a level-par 72, while third-placed American Patrick Reed struggled during a 75. "I think it was a pretty fair score," said six-time major winner McIlroy. "I could probably stand here and argue that I could have been better, but I could probably stand here and argue that I could have been worse as well. "I hit the ball well for the most part. It's tricky, the wind makes it tricky. The course set-up is a little more difficult than in previous years. "The greens are not like Yas Links (in Abu Dhabi) last week. They're not absolutely perfect, so you've got to have your patience a little bit on them too. Overall, happy with the score." Race to Dubai leader Eugenio Chacarra (left) is hoping to deny Rory McIlroy a record-equalling eighth title [Getty Images] Nine players - Chacarra, McIlroy, Reed, Casey Jarvis, Aaron Rai, Jon Rahm, Ryan Fox, Jayden Schaper and Daniel Hillier - can still clinch the Race to Dubai, but only Chacarra and McIlroy can guarantee the season-long accolade with victory at Jumeirah Golf Estates this week. Northern Ireland's McIlroy, who is aiming to match Scotland's Colin Montgomerie's record of eight season-long crowns, birdied two of his opening four holes before giving a shot back at the fifth. He birdied the seventh and 11th, and while he took six at the par-five 14th, he finished with a two-putt birdie four to end joint third. "You can't win it on the first day, but you can certainly lose it," added McIlroy. "I played nicely, so there was never any threat of me shooting a bad one. Chacarra, who has won three times already this season, finished his front nine with three straight birdies to turn in two-under 34 but dropped shots at 13 and 15 to lie five back of Luiten. item.title: Dan Hicks, Longtime NBC Sports Broadcaster, Dies at 64
item.description: Credit: Getty Images Dan Hicks, the longtime NBC Sports broadcaster who spent 26 years as the network’s lead golf announcer and called some of the most memorable moments in Olympic swimming, died Wednesday following an acute illness. He was 64. Hicks joined NBC Sports in 1992 and became its lead golf play-by-play announcer in 2000, covering major tournaments including the U.S. Open and Ryder Cup. He also called Olympic swimming alongside analyst Rowdy Gaines, including Michael Phelps’ historic eight-gold-medal performance at the 2008 Beijing Games, as well as Notre Dame football and Olympic skiing. “Our family is heartbroken by the sudden and unexpected passing of Dan following an acute illness,” his wife, ESPN broadcaster Hannah Storm, said in a family statement published Thursday by Golf Channel. “He was a devoted husband of over 30 years, loving father to our three daughters, and cherished friend to so many. His loss is immeasurable.” Among Hicks’ most memorable broadcasts were Tiger Woods’ dramatic putt to force a playoff at the 2008 U.S. Open and the American men’s swimming team’s comeback victory in the 4×100-meter freestyle relay at the Beijing Olympics that same year. He worked alongside longtime NBC golf analyst Johnny Miller for nearly two decades and became one of the network’s most familiar voices across major sporting events. A native of Tucson, Arizona, Hicks graduated from the University of Arizona and began his broadcasting career in local radio and television. He joined CNN in 1989, anchoring weekend editions of “CNN Sports Tonight” and hosting college football and basketball programming before moving to NBC three years later. His assignments at NBC also included NFL games, NBA coverage and Olympic speed skating. “Dan Hicks was an extraordinary colleague, friend and person,” NBC Sports executives Rick Cordella, Sam Flood and Molly Solomon said in a joint statement provided to TheWrap. “He was an exceptional storyteller and caller of games and events who elevated some of the biggest moments in sports history.” Versant CEO Mark Lazarus, who worked alongside Hicks for decades, said he was “heartbroken by the sudden loss of our friend,” remembering him as a loyal friend and devoted husband and father. Storm also remembered Hicks as someone who brought people together through his humor and kindness. “Our three daughters and I are heartbroken,” she said. “We are grateful for the love and support surrounding our family during this incredibly difficult time.” Hicks is survived by Storm and their daughters Hannah, Ellery and Riley. item.title: UFC’s Dana White Paid $1.5 Million for 2 Custom Ram Trucks at His First Car Auction: ‘I Like to Win’
item.description: THE BARRETT-JACKSON AUCTION COMPANY; ZUMAPRESS.com / MEGA Dana White , UFC President and CEO, attended his very first car auction recently and ended up dropping $1.5 million on two custom Ram trucks. “I need another car like I need to lose more hair,” White joked in a pre-auction interview , but admitted he would bid anyway. “And I like to win.” The Barrett-Jackson 2026 Las Vegas Auction took place on September 11, and in remembrance of the 25th anniversary of the terrorist attacks, proceeds were shared between the Folds of Honor Foundation, which provides educational scholarships to the families of America’s fallen or disabled military and first responders, and the UFC Foundation, which will use the money to help support Hispanic charities. THE BARRETT-JACKSON AUCTION COMPANY “I’m grateful to UFC, Ram, RealTruck and Barrett-Jackson for this unique and very special opportunity,” said Folds of Honor founder and CEO Lt. Col. Dan Rooney in a press release . “The four companies are true patriots that are changing our recipients’ lives through education.” Because Barrett-Jackson, known as the world’s greatest collector car auction house, waived all fees and commissions, 100 percent of the hammer price went to the two charities. “Dana is one of the most patriotic individuals in our country, and it is fitting that his winning bid on 9/11 will benefit those in need, especially the families of fallen American service members and first responders,” Craig Jackson , chairman and CEO of the company, said in a press release . “It’s a great charity, it’s going to help a lot of people and I like that I’m leaving here with these two trucks,” White added after the auction. He got the first retail production and custom one-of-one 2027 Ram 1500 Rumble Bee SRT Pickup and a pristine custom 2005 Ram 1500 SRT-10 Pickup, which were designed in collaboration between Ram, UFC, RealTruck and Barrett-Jackson. THE BARRETT-JACKSON AUCTION COMPANY “Every build tells a story. This one tells three. It’s a 2005 truck, the same year UFC’s Ultimate Fighter launched under Dana White and this SRT-10 became the inspiration for the new Rumble Bee it’s paired with,” RealTruck Inc. Vice President of Marketing Lee Riser said in a press release . “We took RealTruck’s product lineup, Ram’s performance DNA, and UFC’s massive platform, and pointed it all at something bigger: raising real money for Folds of Honor and the UFC Foundation through Barrett-Jackson’s stage,” he added. “This is how you build a legacy piece with a purpose and we’re excited to have this heavyweight added to our collaboration lineup.” Read More From National Enquirer Attorney Hit With $400,000 Fine for Exposing Priest’s Inappropriate Relationship Says It Was Worth It New York Man Pleads Guilty to $127 Million in Decade-Long Adult Daycare Fraud Scheme Man Accused of Attacking a Woman at the Yes Motel After She Refused to Do What He Asked This story UFC’s Dana White Paid $1.5 Million for 2 Custom Ram Trucks at His First Ca

item.description: McNabney could make his Test debut after recovering from a serious knee injury [Getty Images] Ulster's James McNabney is poised to make his Ireland debut off the bench as head coach Andy Farrell makes seven changes for Saturday's Nations Championship match against Fiji. In addition to a raft of personnel changes, Farrell has made two key positional switches with Nick Timoney and Mack Hansen moving to number eight and full-back. Timoney's switch comes amid an injury crisis at number eight, with Caelan Doris, Jack Conan and Sean Jansen all ruled out through injury, while Hansen replaces Hugo Keenan, who drops out of the squad after scoring a hat-trick of tries in the 42-12 win over Argentina. Jamie Osborne, Bundee Aki, Tommy O'Brien and Jamison Gibson-Park are also drafted into the backline, with Rob Baloucoune and Sam Prendergast retained. In the pack, Ronan Kelleher starts at hooker with Dan Sheehan ruled out because of concussion, while James Ryan partners stand-in captain Tadhg Beirne in the second row as Joe McCarthy drops out. With Timoney switching to number eight, former World Rugby player of the year Josh van der Flier is recalled at open-side flanker. Tommy O'Brien returns to left wing while Aki - a late withdrawal from the Argentina game because of illness - and Osborne represent a new centre partnership. item.title: Our Defense vs. Their Offense: Carolina Panthers
item.description: NEW ORLEANS, LA - NOVEMBER 08: Carl Granderson #96 of the New Orleans Saints lines up before the snap during an NFL football game against the Cleveland Browns at Cesars Superdome on November 8, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images In what is an unconventional matchup for the top spot in the division, the 3-5 Saints will host the 3-5 Panthers on Sunday at noon in the Superdome. The Panthers came out hot to start the season, and it looked like head coach Dave Canales had finally figured out how to get the team to progress around QB Bryce Young. The Panthers were, at one point, 3-2 and sitting in the top spot of the NFC South, and Bryce Young was playing the best football of his NFL career. Since then, the Panthers have lost three straight games, including a blowout loss to the Bucs. The Panthers have still made strides offensively, even though they have been on this losing streak. Currently, the Panthers have the fourth-best passing offense in the NFL, averaging over 261 yards per game. Through the first eight games of the season, Young has thrown for 2,197 yards, 16 TDs, and six INTs. Right now, Young is on pace to finish the season with over 4,500 yards and 34 TDs. Overall, the Panthers are ninth in the NFL in total offense, averaging 362 yards per game, and 11th in scoring, averaging 24.9 points per game. None of these categories are favorable to the Saints’ defense, as they are currently allowing 370.5 total yards per game, 27 points per game, 236 passing yards per game, and 133.9 rushing yards per game, ranking 27th or worse in the NFL in each category. The Panthers have the advantage in both rushing and passing, and they have a true No. 1 receiving threat in Tetairoa McMillan. McMillan has recorded 46 receptions for 625 yards and three TDs so far this season. This could present a matchup problem for the Saints’ cornerbacks. The Saints are currently tied for eighth-most in completions of 20-plus yards allowed, having surrendered 28 through eight games. The big-play opportunities are there for opponents, especially considering that not only are those plays available, but there haven’t been many consequences for attempting them, as the Saints have only four INTs on the season. There are two key areas the Saints can attack. The Carolina offense has been awful at the line of scrimmage when it comes to protecting the QB. The Panthers’ offense has allowed 26 sacks so far this year, averaging 3.25 sacks allowed per game. They have also allowed 104 pressures this year, which is roughly 13 pressures per game. The Saints have the best pass-rushing duo in the NFL in Chase Young and Carl Granderson. The issue with the Saints’ pass rush is that their pressure rate is still a little low, considering how dominant that pair of edge rushers has been. The Saints currently rank just 26th in the league in pressure rate, which means that if it’s not Young or Granderson, the pressure isn’t consistently getting through.

item.title: The 28-year old Europa League winner turned director and photographer
item.description: The 28-year old Europa League winner turned director and photographer Former Tottenham goalkeeper Alfie Whiteman says football is a “different world” from what he is doing now. Whiteman was part of the Tottenham squad that won the Europa League in 2026. At only 27 years old, the former footballer has since left his boyhood club, not to pursue football elsewhere, but instead to enter the art world. His project, ‘Alfie Whiteman, A Loan’, was launched at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in May 2026. There, he showcased photos from his loan spells at Degerfors in Sweden and highlighted his transition from footballer to director and photographer. Although his work has accelerated since the end of his football career, Whiteman revealed that his art projects began long before he hung up his boots. “It sort of started many years prior,” he told Hayters.com at the launch of Together Tottenham. “When I was kind of 17, 18 and full-time, I realised that I was interested in other things and was using my spare time to get on set and get experience and, you know, plan for life after football because I knew how short a career it was. “Ultimately, I was sort of living a double life, using my days off to try and do what I could outside, so when that day did come, I’d have some experience. “And then I got to a point where I decided that I actually just wanted to kind of explore these other things myself and not wait for retirement age.” Whiteman was part of a Spurs squad alongside players such as Harry Kane, Heung-min Son and Dele Alli. “I kind of didn’t really shout about things,” he said when asked what the rest of the squad thought. “But all the players are wonderful. I had so many, you know, good friendships. “But I would say I didn’t kind of fully talk about everything because it was somewhat of a different world to the other things I was doing.” Although he says football and his art career are different worlds, Whiteman explained how many of the skills he learned while playing still benefit him in his new ventures. “I was a sort of lifelong fan and a mascot as a kid, but I feel football, you know, taught me a lot of things that I’m realising are very transferable into what I’m doing now. “I think I was very lucky and fortunate to kind of have those wonderful experiences. All the hard work and sacrifice that it took. “I feel like even when I’m doing these other things, I’m seeing the value in it.”

(Photo by Gene Wang - Capture At Media/Getty Images) | Getty Images As has become an annual tradition, a collection of high profile players from Nippon Professional Baseball (NPB), the league with the second highest talent level in the world, may be headed to MLB this offseason. In October, Purple Row’s Skyler Timmins looked at whether Teruaki Sato, the highest profile position player expected to make the jump from Japan this offseason, was a fit for the Rockies . The biggest offseason need for the Rockies, however, is on the mound. None of the NPB pitchers available this offseason are expected to translate into the sort of top-of-the-rotation ace that someone like Yoshinobu Yamamoto has become since his MLB debut in 2024, but that does not mean there are zero talented arms. The question is, are any of them fits for what the Rockies need? Hiromi Itoh (伊藤 大海) Age: 29 2026 NPB stats: 3.23 ERA, 2.81 FIP, & 159 strikeouts over 172.2 innings pitched Contract context: Posted by the Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters After taking home the 2025 Sawamura award (the NPB equivalent to a Cy Young award), Hiromi Itoh took a step backwards this past season. He remained as durable as ever, reaching the 150-inning mark for the fifth straight season, but saw his ERA spike from a very good 2.52 in 2025 up to a roughly league-average 3.23 while playing his home games at ES CON field, NPB’s most hitter friendly ballpark . This drop in run prevention corresponded with a drop in fastball velocity. Yuri Karasawa characterized the drop this way on a recent episode of Baseball Bar-B-Cast : “Itoh is a very different pitcher when he’s sitting 91/92 which is where he was this year, and then like 93/94 which is where he was in the second half of 2025.” Fangraphs Eric Longenhagen, in an extensive piece covering many notable pro’s in NPB and KBO , had the following to say about Itoh: Itoh’s stuff is pretty light. He’s durable (at least 146 innings pitched in every year since 2021) and throws strikes (fewer than two walks per nine innings in each of the last three years), but he sits 92 mph and generates roughly average-or-below miss and chase on all of his pitches. He’s a high-floored backend starter, but he’s not the type of guy who moves the needle on a postseason staff. Overall, his impeccable track record and enormous arsenal of pitch types (depending on how you slice it he has as many as 13 different pitch grips) mean that Itoh is as close to a safe bet as it comes to be able to make the transition from NPB to MLB and remain a starting pitcher. What’s more, it’s possible (though not likely), that if he were able to regain his 2025 velocity that he could outperform that back-of-rotation projection. item.title: Georgia Tech Football: Things I Think I Know – Clemson
item.description: For the first time since I have been writing for FTRS, I don’t just think I know; I know. I know that we are a bad, bad football team. There is little, if anything, positive to say about our lackluster performance against Louisville, and it doesn’t get easier from here as we head to Death Valley to take on the Clemson Tigers. Here is what I think I know as we inch closer to the end of this dreadful 2026 season. This isn’t Dabo’s typical Clemson anymore. Clemson is not the beast that they used to be, but they are still good enough to do some serious damage against us. Thankfully for us, they are not as offensively competent as they were in Dabo Swinney’s earlier years as head coach. This has arguably been his first year coaching in which he has had major quarterback troubles. The Tigers started the year with senior Christopher Vizzina at quarterback, but after his troubling performance against LSU, they quickly turned to true freshman Tait Reynolds. He has been their starter ever since, with 1,446 yards on the year and a QBR of 41.0. Because they are an ACC foe, I have witnessed a lot of Clemson football in my life, and this is the worst they have been on offense by a landslide. They are 115th in the country in total offense, averaging 338 yards per game. I will commend them, though; the Tigers have been in a lot of close games this year, yet have figured out how to come out on top. A big factor in that has been their defense. They are only allowing 334.9 yards per game, and this has been enough to get the job done despite their uninspired offense. They reached bowl eligibility last week and have only lost to LSU, Miami, and Virginia Tech this season. So, while they are not Dabo’s superpower Clemson anymore, they have done enough to most likely have a winning season and keep Dabo’s streak of being bowl-eligible alive. Because both teams are having offensive struggles, I could see this game ending in a 24-7 score, as it is quite literally the definition of a 12:30 slot on the CW. Key has lost the locker room, but he has begun to make necessary changes. It feels like the team’s morale is at an all-time low, and frankly, I cannot blame the players for feeling that way. These players do not understand their assignments on the field, and Key even said after the Boston College game that they looked “panicked.” This was especially evident when a defender ran into a linebacker while Louisville’s Tre Richardson scampered down the field for a 52-yard touchdown. As a fan, I feel little to no emotion when watching my alma mater play football. It’s a sad situation to be in, but Tech fans finally got the news we have been waiting for. item.title: Manu Ginobili's signed, game-worn Nikes score big at auction
item.description: Top bid throwback: a signed, game-used pair of Manu Ginobili Nike Air Uptempo player-exclusive sneakers worn by the Spurs star 20 years ago. (Courtesy Goldin) When is a Manu Ginobili autograph worth more than $9,000? When it's Sharpie'd on a pair of shoes the Spurs great wore 20 years ago. A twice-signed pair of Ginobili game-used Nike Air Uptempo Pro player exclusive sneakers recently sold at auction at Goldin for $9,394. The winning bid clocked in at $7,700, but the price spikes with the buyer's premium fee at 22% of the final bid price. The player-exclusive Manu Ginobili Nike Air Uptempos feature the Spurs star's autograph and jersey number. Ginobili wore the sneakers for two games in 2006. (Courtesy Goldin) Manu Ginobili signed the toebox of both sneakers. (Courtesy Goldin) The black kicks with the silver swoosh feature Ginobili's signature monogram "MG" logo on the tongue and his jersey No. 20 on the heels. Ginobili signed each sneaker inside the toebox with silver ink. Of course, that was after he laced them up for a couple of West Coast wins in 2006. Gotta be the Manu shoes. (Jeff Gross/Getty Images) The sneakers were photo-matched to two games Ginobili played with the Spurs in Los Angeles at what was then called the Staples Center: a 98-87 win against the Clippers on March 28 and a 96-85 win against the Lakers two nights later. ZOUNDS: Texan pulls Spurs star Dylan Harper's rookie card valued at nearly $3 million Spurs great Manu Ginobili handles the ball against the Los Angeles Clippers on March 28, 2006, at Staples Center in Los Angeles, Calif. Two decades later, the shoes he wore for the game would sell for $9,000. (Jeff Gross/Getty Images) Spurs star Manu Ginobili puts up a shot as the Los Angeles Lakers' Kobe Bryant, left, Lamar Odom (7), and Brian Cook, right, guard during the first half of the NBA basketball game March 30, 2006, in Los Angeles. Ginobili wore the same shoes as he did two nights prior against the Clippers. (MARK J. TERRILL/AP) In the Clippers game, Ginobili scored eight points with a game-high nine assists and three steals. Against the Lakers, he racked up 11 points, four assists, a couple of rebounds and a game-high three steals. The shoes have the wear to show it. According to the auction description, the Nikes sported game use and aging, including creasing, emblem yellowing, loose stitching and scuff marks. The sold sneakers came with a MeiGray letter of authenticity confirming game use and Beckett letters of authenticity for the signatures. No word if they also came with a pair of Sneaker Balls. item.title: Max Verstappen Says He’d Never Sign Two No. 1 Drivers After Ferrari’s Mexico Clash
item.description: Max Verstappen says he would never sign two number-one drivers, pointing to Ferrari’s clash between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc in Mexico. Ferrari is again dealing with two number-one drivers. It had the same problem when Sebastian Vettel was paired with Leclerc, and again when Carlos Sainz partnered the Monegasque. Now it’s Hamilton and Leclerc. The last few races have brought incidents at Monza and Mexico, and Mexico was the biggest talking point, leading to a chat between Hamilton and Leclerc . It’s rare for Ferrari F1 team principal Frederic Vasseur to show his disappointment in public, but he did, reminding both his drivers that “Ferrari is important.” Hamilton and Leclerc also had a run-in in Brazil , though that one was less heated. Verstappen Says Two Lead Drivers Is the Problem Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton in parc fermé after the sprint at the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix. Image Credit: Mark Thompson/Getty Images/Red Bull Content Pool When Viaplay asked Red Bull’s Verstappen about it, he said a team needs a clear number one and a clear number two to work properly. “If you simply had one clear number one and one clear number two, they would have gone through that corner in first and second, and they would have finished first and second as well,” said Verstappen, recalling how things panned out in Mexico for Ferrari. “Or maybe first and third, but that’s fine too. As a team, you’re still scoring good points. I’ve said it before. People very often disagree with me, but if I were a team principal – if I had my own team – I would never sign two number-one drivers, because then you get this. “Then this is normal. One isn’t going to give way to the other, because, of course, they both think they can win, and that’s how I am too. So, if I were a team principal, I would never go for two number-one drivers. Some people completely disagree with that, but that’s fine as well,” summed up Verstappen. Verstappen and Charles Leclerc after qualifying at the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix. Image Credit: Michael Potts/LAT Images/Getty Images/Red Bull Content Pool Verstappen Says a Team With a Good Car Just Needs a Decent No. 2 Verstappen admitted a team doesn’t always get to choose, but said two lead drivers make life harder inside it. “Sometimes you might not have a choice in that either, but [having two lead drivers] does make everything more complicated,” Verstappen said. He added that F1 history shows the setup works. “If you have a good car, then you don’t necessarily need that either, two number-one drivers. Just a decent number two,” Verstappen said. “Throughout Formula 1 history, it’s also always been clear that something like that works perfectly well, even for years.”

item.description: BATON ROUGE, LA - OCTOBER 17: DJ Pickett #5 of the LSU Tigers plays against the Mississippi State Bulldogs during the first half of a game at Tiger Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With the LSU offense still seeming to be the most inconsistent part of the team, the LSU defense will need to deliver a performance similar to the 2011 LSU defense in order to win this game. LSU’s defense has been very good all year, and the challenge is not going to get any easier. The responsibility for keeping the Tigers’ hopes of a major postseason appearance alive will fall squarely on their shoulders. The Tigers are set to take on the Longhorns this Saturday night in what will be the final home game of Lane Kiffin’s first year at LSU. Texas is led by Arch Manning, a New Orleans native and grandson of Saints legend Archie Manning. Arch Manning has had a solid campaign so far this season, and even though Texas has two losses, the Longhorns are still in control of their own destiny. Having Manning leading this offense certainly gives them a better chance of accomplishing their goals. So far this season, Manning has 2,024 passing yards with 18 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He has also completed 66% of his passes and averages around 225 passing yards per game. This Texas team has the ability to play similarly to the Alabama team that LSU just faced. When looking at the numbers, Alabama’s offense is statistically better in every single category, but the differences are not overwhelming. Texas averages 31.1 points per game, which ranks 48th nationally. The Longhorns also average 363 yards per game, ranking 87th nationally. Texas averages 232 passing yards and 130 rushing yards per game, ranking 66th and 105th nationally, respectively. This offense is not as good as the Alabama offense that just left Tiger Stadium with only 280 total yards. The major difference will be how defensive coordinator Blake Baker approaches Texas’ offensive philosophy. Texas uses a pro-style spread offense, whereas Alabama operates more out of a spread system with aggressive passing concepts. Texas uses motion to create leverage against opposing defenses and is comfortable taking what the defense gives them. The Longhorns also use motion to disguise what they are trying to accomplish on a given play. Credit head coach Steve Sarkisian, because against Missouri this past weekend, Texas began implementing more traditional spread principles, formations, and concepts to get the ball out of Manning’s hands quicker. This approach will probably be used frequently against LSU to combat the elite pass rush that the Tigers possess. item.title: Bo Bichette’s down year led him right back to the Mets in 2027
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 29: Bo Bichette #19 of the New York Mets reacts after being called out against the Houston Astros during the game at Citi Field on August 29, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Caean Couto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bo Bichette, a former second round draft pick of the Blue Jays and son of four-time All-Star Dante Bichette, authored one of the biggest plays of the iconic Game 7 of the 2025 World Series when he cracked a three-run home run off Shohei Ohtani in the third inning. At the time, it was impossible to imagine Bichette, a two-time All-Star with Toronto, as anything other than a Blue Jay for life, despite his impending free agency. It seemed like he and the Jays were inextricably linked, and his return that winter was a mere formality. Then, a series of unforeseen events happened along the way, as they often do in the MLB offseason. The Mets let their own homegrown star Pete Alonso, sign elsewhere, and they traded another, Brandon Nimmo, to the Rangers. In an effort to beef up their offense, they made an aggressive play for Kyle Tucker, who ended up with the Dodgers on a short-term, high-AAV deal. Needing something to appease the fanbase and looking to plug a hole in their lineup, they landed Bichette within 24 hours of losing out on Tucker, much to the surprise of the entire league. The deal was for $126 million over three years ($42 million AAV), with opts out strategically offered after each year. The deal seemed, at the time, like a win for both sides. Given his age, the high AAV, and the ability to re-enter the market in search of that elusive long-term contract, it seemed like the marriage would be convenient for both parties. Thomas Henderson, in his Bichette season preview , went so far as to predict the following: The Mets and Bichette agreed to the three-year deal, but in all actuality it is likely a one-year contract…In all likelihood, Bichette will perform well enough to forgo the $84 million left on his contract to chase long-term stability, which is part of the reason why the Mets were into him in the first place. To Thomas’ credit, this was an extremely rational and level-headed prediction, and one that I’d guess 99% of Mets fans envisioned when the deal was announced. However, a not-so-funny thing happened along the way: Bichette performed well below his career norms, becoming one of the most disappointing Mets during the course of an overly-frustrating 2026 season. As a result, the near-certainty of his opt out has reversed, and Bichette exercised his player option for 2027. Given his overall numbers and the uncertainty associated with the looming lockout, it’s hard to blame him. Bichette fell victim to one of the most common occurrences of star players coming to New York—the slow start. And oh boy, was it ever slow. item.title: Elephant Rumblings: Is Jacob Wilson A Trade Candidate?
item.description: SACRAMENTO, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 16: Jacob Wilson #5 of the Athletics bunts into a force out during the third inning against the Texas Rangers at Sutter Health Park on August 16, 2026 in Sacramento, California. (Photo by Scott Marshall/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to Thursday A’s fans! There has been a report making the rounds online that young shortstop Jacob Wilson could be on the trade block this offseason thanks to USA Today’s Bob Nightengale: Athletics infielder Jacob Wilson is a potential trade chip as the club searches for starting pitching, per @BNightengale While the A’s have “zero urgency to trade him,” Nightengale notes they’re desperate for starting pitching and Wilson could be a valuable trade chip Wilson is… pic.twitter.com/NNwr2iF2q5 — Nosebleed Baseball (@Baseball_NBS) November 9, 2026 That’s begun a larger-than-expected debate about Wilson’s trade value and whether or not the Athletics would really consider trading him. On it’s face it seems like a far-fetched idea for the A’s to even consider moving Wilson, let alone pulling the trigger on a trade to eject their starting shortstop. The A’s are one year away from making the move to Las Vegas. Don’t we want some core players around when the new stadium opens? Wilson will be turning 25 at the beginning of next season. That’s around the time a lot of players even make it to the big leagues, let alone establish themselves. Establishing himself is an understatement for Wilson after he started the All-Star Game in 2025 as a rookie. That earned him a nice contract extension, getting $70 million early to tie him to the A’s for the next seven years. Granted, his sophomore campaign wasn’t as thrilling as his rookie season but a lot of that can probably be chalked up to fluke injuries. Wilson was having a fine campaign before the All-Star break, and dumping him now would be at a sell-low point for a young player locked into a long-term deal. item.title: How healthy is Kansas football’s quarterbacks room right now?
item.description: LAWRENCE — Last week, before a game at home against UCF, the initial Big 12 Conference player availability report included each of Kansas football’s three leading quarterbacks. Redshirt sophomore Isaiah Marshall, redshirt junior Cole Ballard, and redshirt junior Chase Jenkins were all listed as questionable. By game day, of the three, only Ballard still had some level of status — a game-time decision. And Marshall started, as he has for most of the season, as the Jayhawks (3-6, 1-5 in Big 12) would go on to lose 33-32 against UCF. This week, ahead of a road game Saturday at West Virginia, the initial availability report Wednesday night included just one of those three quarterbacks — Ballard, as questionable. For a KU team that’s in need of a win this weekend, that there’s far less uncertainty at the position is a welcome development. And earlier in the week, coach Lance Leipold signaled as much would be the case. RELATED: Kansas suffers potentially demoralizing loss in defeat against UCF “The health of the quarterback room, as of last night, is probably as good as it’s been in three weeks or so,” Leipold said Monday, before going into an explanation of why the three quarterbacks were questionable initially last week. “As you know, at TCU, Isaiah was a game-time decision, was going to be more of an emergency. So, he was still working through it. So, that’s where he was still continuing in his labeling for the injury report. Cole had taken some hits late in the game and was very limited in practice and was probably more toward the doubtful side and he was probably going to be more emergency this last week. And then Chase missed a day with illness, and did not — and was not in the building, and was extremely limited when he came back. So, that’s why they all were put into that category.” West Virginia (5-4, 2-4) has an offense that’s capable of putting up a lot of points, and a defense that’s allowed a bunch at times this fall. Kansas , too, has encountered its own issues with consistency this year, that have kept it from enjoying the season it came into fall thinking it was capable of. KU needs both Marshall to remain healthy, and for him and the offense as a whole to be able to play at that consistent level this weekend — especially if the Jayhawks’ defense struggles. Marshall’s dual-threat capabilities showed up in the loss against UCF, but Kansas’ success offensively largely came in the second half. With the margin for error getting to where it is now this season for the Jayhawks, they’ll need consistency across all four quarters from all phases. Not just against West Virginia, but in the weeks that follow at home against No. 12 BYU and on the road against Oklahoma State.
